I'm the sales employee who handles the quotation process. I receive the request, check the customer information, create the quotation, and send it to the customer.
I don't know who sends the request or what it contains. I just receive it and start from there.
When I check the customer information, I look it up in the CRM. That's where I get the customer details from.
To create the quotation, I use the quoting system. I pull the customer information and the pricing information from there to put together the quotation.
I send the quotation to the customer by email. After that, at month-end, I also send a summary of the quotation information to Accounting using Excel.
I don't know why checking the customer information is necessary. I just do it as part of the process.
I don't know why creating the quotation is necessary. I just do it as part of the process.

I don't know why receiving the quotation request is necessary. I just do it as part of the process.
I don't know of any special cases or different paths in the process. It's just the steps I described.
Yes, the quotation I create is the same document I send to the customer by email.

I don't know if the customer information I check in the CRM is the same as the customer information I pull from the quoting system when creating the quotation. I just use the customer information in each system as part of the process.
